takeaway_view: A small gap to a 60/40 benchmark is what two index-fund mixes should produce. Stocks did the work; bonds gave little cushion.

theme_evidence: USD/CAD fell from {fx0} to {fx1} ({fx_chg}): a US dollar bought fewer Canadian dollars at month-end. [boc_valet]
Unhedged US, international and emerging-market ETFs are {foreign_w} of the portfolio and report in CAD after currency moves. XUU returned {ret_XUU}. [prices]
On July 15 the Bank of Canada linked earlier Canadian-dollar weakness to higher US than Canadian yields. These sources do not establish why the currency firmed in August. [boc_2026_07_15]
theme_view: Illustration only: if XUU's US assets earned about {fx_implied} in US dollars, the currency move took roughly {fx_drag} off the CAD return (indicative: ETF closes and daily-average rates differ in timing). Unhedged exposure is a deliberate diversifier: it adds return when the Canadian dollar weakens and trims it when it firms. One month does not argue for changing it.
equity_view: Canada ({ret_XIC}) and emerging markets ({ret_XEC}) led. US ({ret_XUU}) and developed international ({ret_XEF}) gained less in CAD. The sleeve ended at {eq_end_w} of the portfolio, {eq_drift} above target.
fi_view: Canada's 2-year yield rose {y2_chg} and the 10-year {y10_chg}, lowering bond prices. Distributions offset most of it: XBB returned {ret_XBB} against {pr_XBB} in price. The sleeve finished at {fi_sleeve}. [prices][boc_valet]
rebalance: Maintain. The largest holding drift is {max_hold_drift} (band {hold_band}); the largest sleeve drift is {max_class_drift} (band {class_band}). No trade triggers, so drifted weights carry into September. A reset would trade {turnover} of the portfolio.
counter: For acting: yields are rising, three FOMC members preferred a hike on July 29 [fed_2026_07_29], and bonds gave no cushion. For patience: drift is inside the bands and one month of yields is weak evidence of a trend.
risks: Rates: further yield rises would hurt bonds. [boc_valet]
Currency: a firmer Canadian dollar trims the {foreign_w} unhedged foreign assets.
Policy and trade: Middle East war and US trade policy. [boc_2026_07_15]
methodology: Total return: closing prices, distributions reinvested at the ex-date close, net of fund expenses. Weights are beginning-of-month, set to target at the {start_label} close. Contribution is weight times return, not formal attribution. Foreign-market ETFs are CAD-listed, so no currency conversion is applied.

notes: Main message. In August 2026 the hypothetical 60/40 portfolio returned {port} in Canadian dollars and the benchmark returned {bench}. Equities contributed {eq_contrib} and bonds {fi_contrib}. The chart shows cumulative total return from the July 31 close. The theme is currency: USD/CAD fell from {fx0} to {fx1}, which trims what unhedged foreign equities earn for a Canadian investor. For a client: stocks rose, bonds were flat, and a stronger Canadian dollar took a little off foreign holdings. Sources are the exchange closes and Bank of Canada series listed in the report.

Portfolio implications. Canadian equities and emerging markets led. The equity sleeve ended at {eq_end_w} against a 60% target. Bond yields rose modestly, so price losses on the broad bond fund were mostly offset by distributions. The illustrative rule says maintain: the largest drift is {max_hold_drift}, inside the {hold_band} band. Resetting to target would trade {turnover} of the portfolio. This is an illustration of a rule, not advice for any client.

Risks and monitoring. Rates are the main risk: three FOMC members preferred a rise on July 29 and Canadian yields moved up in August. Currency risk is two-way. The Bank of Canada has flagged the Middle East war and US trade policy. Next events: the Bank of Canada decision on September 2 and the FOMC meeting on September 15 and 16. The counterargument is that a more defensive investor could act now; the case for patience is that drift is small and one month of yields is weak evidence.
